transcripts.name: enroll-and-hello
transcripts.description: A new device enrolls with the account's password and keeps the token; every later stream opens with hello. The first envelope after welcome fixes the stream's role: a keepalive makes it the control stream.

transcripts.name: clipboard
transcripts.description: The clipboard on the server: one value per member account, in memory only, the latest complete upload the value. A put declares kind and size on a data stream, the server answers clipboard-ready, the sender writes exactly size raw bytes - no frames, no chunk headers - and the server answers clipboard-stored (clipId, sha256, storedAt) and closes. A get answers the members and the bytes; clipboard-info on the control stream answers the members alone. `welcome.features` carries `clipboard`.

transcripts.name: sealed-devices
transcripts.description: The device key of DEVICE-EXCHANGE 27 item DF on a server that advertises `sealed` (item DP): a device enrolls or registers with the capability `e2e-v1` and an `e2eKey` (`{v:1, kem}`, a P-256 point); `enrolled` and `welcome` list the feature `sealed`; the key is part of the device's record, listed to every device of the account and pushed in `changed`; a device that predates the capability sends neither and its record carries no key; a known deviceId enrolls again with its own key (a token rotation) or not at all (id-collision).

steps.note: `enrolled.features` lists `sealed`: the server keeps and delivers the device key, the boxes and the sealed clipboard kind (item DP)

the tablet is online now

the device is kept as it was; a stranger who learnt the password cannot put a key of its own under a known deviceId
the rotation is a change of the record (its token and name are rewritten), and the key stays the same

transcripts.name: sealed-clipboard
transcripts.description: The sealed clipboard of DEVICE-EXCHANGE 27 item DN on the slot of section 22: a put declares `kind` `sealed`, `size` the number of sealed bytes and `sealed` the box with the context `clipboard` (its payload holds kind, mimeType, size and sha256 of the clear value; a sealed put carries no mimeType and no name in clear); the sealed bytes follow `clipboard-ready` raw; the server counts, hashes and stores the sealed bytes and answers `clipboard-state` and `clipboard-value` with `kind` `sealed` and the box, byte for byte. A sealed put with no box, or one that names the value in clear, is not an envelope the codec reads: it is malformed, the stream is closed with no answer, and no transcript can hold it.
